name: JSDoc for Public APIs
description: Require JSDoc comments on all exported functions, classes, and interfaces for discoverability and IDE support.
content:
# JSDoc for Public APIs Rules

- Add JSDoc comments to every exported function, class, interface, and type alias — these are your public API
- Include a one-sentence description of what the function does — start with a verb ("Returns", "Validates", "Creates")
- Document all parameters with `@param` — include the type (if not using TypeScript), name, and description
- Document the return value with `@returns` — describe what is returned and under what conditions
- Use `@throws` to document exceptions — list error types and the conditions that cause them
- Use `@example` to show usage — a code example is worth more than a paragraph of description
- Use `@deprecated` with a migration path — "Use `newFunction()` instead" not just "Deprecated"
- Document complex types inline — `@param {Object} options` with nested `@param {string} options.name`
- Don't document obvious things — `@param name The name` adds no value, describe what it's used for
- Keep JSDoc in sync with the code — outdated documentation is worse than no documentation
- Use `@see` to link related functions, classes, or external documentation
- Configure ESLint with `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` to enforce JSDoc on exports — make it a CI check
